ai.literal: And espionage and the renowned treatise, these both, let one say, are the eyes of the king.
ai.translation: Espionage and the renowned books of law—these two, let one say, are the eyes of a king.
ai.modern: ஒற்றனும் புகழ்பெற்ற அறநூலும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டையும் அரசனது கண்கள் என்று சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the two essential tools a ruler needs to govern effectively. The poet states that espionage (the spy system) and the renowned treatises of law and statecraft are the two eyes of a king. While the books of law provide the ethical and theoretical framework for governance, the spies provide real-time, practical information about the kingdom and its enemies. Together, they allow the ruler to see clearly and make informed decisions, acting as his eyes.

ai.literal: To everyone all things that happen always quickly knowing is the king's duty.
ai.translation: To know quickly and at all times everything that happens to everyone is the duty of a king.
ai.modern: எல்லாருக்கும் நிகழும் எல்லா நிகழ்வுகளையும் எப்போதும் விரைவாகத் தெரிந்து கொள்வது அரசனின் கடமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core responsibility of a ruler regarding state intelligence. The phrase 'ellārkkum ellām nikaḻpavai' emphasizes that a king must be aware of everything happening to all people, not just a select few. The words 'eññāṉṟum' (always) and 'val' (quickly) highlight that this information gathering must be continuous and rapid. Knowing these events swiftly allows the ruler to make timely decisions and protect the kingdom from internal and external threats.

ai.literal: By a spy, having spied, the facts not knowing king, victory to attain, anything lying there is not.
ai.translation: For a king who does not discover the facts of what has happened through his spies, there is no way to achieve victory.
ai.modern: ஒற்றர்களைக் கொண்டு ஆராய்ந்து உண்மைகளைத் தெரிந்து கொள்ளாத அரசனுக்கு, வெற்றி பெறுவதற்கான வழி என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of espionage for a ruler's success. The poet states that a king who fails to use spies to investigate and understand the ground realities (poruḷ) cannot hope for victory (koṟṟam). The phrase 'koḷak kiṭantatu il' strongly asserts that there is absolutely no prospect or possibility of triumph lying ahead for such an uninformed ruler. Thus, intelligence gathering is portrayed as the very foundation of political survival and victory.

ai.literal: Those who do work, one's own relatives, and enemies, thus in that manner, everyone, investigating is espionage.
ai.translation: Espionage consists of watching everyone closely—those who perform state duties, one's own relatives, and one's enemies.
ai.modern: அரசுப் பணிகளைச் செய்பவர்கள், தன் உறவினர்கள், பகைவர்கள் என்று சொல்லப்படும் எல்லாரையும் கண்காணித்து ஆராய்வதே ஒற்றாடல் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the comprehensive scope of a ruler's intelligence network. The poet lists three vital groups that must be kept under surveillance: 'vinai-ceyvār' (officials executing state duties), 'cuṟṟam' (the ruler's own relatives), and 'vēṇṭātār' (declared enemies). By watching officials, the ruler ensures loyalty and efficiency; by watching relatives, internal conspiracies are prevented; and by watching enemies, external threats are anticipated. True espionage ('oṟṟu') leaves no one unobserved, ensuring the stability of the state through complete awareness.

ai.literal: With an unquestioned appearance, not fearing any eye, and never spilling secrets anywhere, is indeed a capable spy.
ai.translation: A capable spy is one who adopts a disguise that raises no suspicion, shows no fear when stared at, and never reveals secrets under any circumstances.
ai.modern: சந்தேகப்படாத தோற்றத்துடன், யாருடைய பார்வைக்கும் அஞ்சாமல், எவ்விடத்திலும் தன் ரகசியங்களை வெளிப்படுத்தாமல் இருக்க வல்லவனே ஒற்றன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three core attributes of a successful spy. First, they must adopt an appearance or disguise ('கடாஅ உரு') that is so natural it raises no questions or suspicion. Second, even when subjected to intense scrutiny or confronted directly, their eyes must show no fear ('கண்ணஞ்சாது'). Finally, they must have the absolute self-control to never let slip ('உகாஅமை') any secrets or their true identity under any circumstances.

ai.literal: Having become those who have the guise of those who have renounced, having entered and investigated, whatever is done to them, a spy is one without slip.
ai.translation: Assuming the guise of holy ascetics, entering everywhere to investigate secrets, a true spy is one who never slips up or reveals their identity, no matter what is done to them.
ai.modern: துறவிகளின் வேடத்தை ஏற்றுக்கொண்டு, பிறர் அறியாதவாறு புகுந்து உண்மைகளை ஆராய்ந்து, தமக்கு என்ன நேர்ந்தாலும் தன் மெய்ம்மையை வெளிப்படுத்தாத சோர்வில்லாத தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே ஒற்றாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the extreme operational methods and resilience required of a spy. A spy should adopt the disguise of ascetics ('துறந்தார் படிவத்தர்') because holy men have free access to all places without raising suspicion. They must enter deep into enemy territory ('இறந்து') to gather intelligence. Most importantly, even if they are caught, tortured, or interrogated ('என் செயினும்'), they must never lose their composure or slip up ('சோர்வு இலது') to betray their mission.

ai.literal: Those things that are hidden to inquire capable of becoming, those things known doubt without having is the spy.
ai.translation: A spy is one who is capable of discovering hidden secrets and who can convey what they have learned without any doubt.
ai.modern: மறைக்கப்பட்ட இரகசியங்களைக் கேட்டறியும் ஆற்றல் உடையவராகி, தான் அறிந்தவற்றைச் சந்தேகத்திற்கு இடமில்லாமல் தெளிவாகத் தெரிவிப்பவரே ஒற்றர் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential attributes of a spy. First, a spy must possess the capability to discover secrets and hidden matters that others try to conceal. Second, the information they gather must be verified so thoroughly that they can report it with absolute certainty, leaving no room for doubt. Thus, the poet emphasizes both the skill of gathering intelligence and the reliability of the gathered facts.

ai.literal: A spy, having spied, the information brought, even that, by another one spy, having verified, should confirm.
ai.translation: Even the information brought by a spy who has investigated must be verified and confirmed through another independent spy.
ai.modern: ஒரு ஒற்றன் ஆராய்ந்து கொண்டு வந்த செய்தியையும், வேறொரு ஒற்றனைக் கொண்டு ஆராய்ந்து உண்மை என்று உறுதி செய்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the necessity of cross-verifying intelligence in statecraft. A ruler must not act immediately on the report of a single spy, as there is always a risk of error, bias, or deception. Instead, the ruler should send a second, independent spy to investigate the same matter. Only when the information brought by the first spy is confirmed by the second spy should it be accepted as the truth. This double-check system ensures the accuracy of crucial state decisions.

ai.literal: Spying on spy without knowing let one employ; together three [spies'] words agreeing, [it] will be confirmed.
ai.translation: Let a ruler employ spies to watch other spies without their knowing each other; when the reports of three such independent spies agree, the information may be accepted as true.
ai.modern: ஒரு ஒற்றனை மற்றொரு ஒற்றன் அறியாதவாறு உளவு பார்க்க ஆள வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு தனித்தனியே உளவு பார்த்த மூன்று ஒற்றர்களின் செய்திகளும் ஒன்றுபட்டால் மட்டுமே அதை உண்மை என்று தெளிந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the method of verifying intelligence gathered by spies. The ruler should employ spies to spy on other spies without them being aware of each other. To ensure the reliability of the information, the ruler must compare the reports of three independent spies. Only when the words of all three spies agree should the information be trusted and acted upon. This system of triple-verification prevents false reports and ensures the security of the state.

ai.literal: Do not bestow honors on a spy in a way that others know; if you do, you become the one who revealed the secret.
ai.translation: Do not honor a spy in a manner that others may know. If you do, you will have revealed your own secret.
ai.modern: ஒற்றனுக்குச் செய்யும் சிறப்புகளைப் பிறர் அறியும்படி செய்யக் கூடாது; அப்படிச் செய்தால், தன் இரகசியத்தைத் தானே வெளிப்படுத்தியவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of maintaining a spy's anonymity. A ruler must never reward or praise a spy in public or in a way that others can observe. If the ruler fails to keep these honors secret, the spy's identity is compromised. Consequently, the ruler himself becomes responsible for exposing his own confidential plans and state secrets to his adversaries.
